alignments.note: Substantival article before a participle supplies the pronoun and nothing else (rule 32); the participle keeps its own relativizer and verb.

The negative is realized by the determiner-negation 'no'. Joining it with the noun as one unit for 'no sin' stays defensible, but the noun is independently recoverable as 'sin' and is not itself a negative, so rules 41 and 59 do not join them and rule 26 splits.
Supplied relativizer is a helper on the participle (rules 7, 32); head on the lexical verb.
The discontinuous frame 'on ... behalf' wraps the phrase and rides undivided with the expressed preposition, headed on the prepositional word (rules 78, 15).
The genitive pronoun carries the possessive inside the frame.
Supplied subject and the supplied 'to be' completing the double-accusative are helpers on the finite verb (rules 7, 9, 11); head on the lexical verb.
The conjunction is realized by the word introducing its English clause (rule 40).
Modal auxiliary rides with its verb; head on the lexical verb (rules 9, 17).
The Greek is anarthrous, so the supplied determiner is an ordinary helper on the noun it determines (rules 51, 58).
Case preposition rides with the noun; head on the noun (rules 21, 17).
